source.title: Revisiting minimum description length complexity in overparameterized models
source.authors: Raaz Dwivedi; Chandan Singh; Bin Yu; M. Wainwright

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some equations and figures are flattened in the web extraction, but the relevant text and figure descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The authors test double-descent behavior in linear regression and argue that it depends on the estimator: OLS can show double or multiple descent, while tuned ridge estimators show a U-shaped curve. They also argue that replacing parameter count with MDL-COMP does not remove the qualitative double-descent pattern.
record.gate_note: The study's own OLS and tuned-ridge test-error curves and its discussion of using MDL-COMP as the complexity axis bear on the claim. Results cited from other papers are not rows. The Prac-MDL-COMP comparisons with CV, ARD, and BIC concern hyperparameter-selection performance, not the claimed curve, and are not included. Appendix B3 varies sample size, but its text does not interpret the plotted OLS curves as showing whether more data raises test error near interpolation.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own linear-regression sweeps over fitted dimension with fixed training data. OLS shows a test-MSE peak and, under a cosine design, multiple peaks. CV- or Prac-MDL-COMP-tuned ridge gives a U-shaped curve. The authors argue the peak comes from a poor estimator, not a mis-counted complexity axis. This bears directly on V4, V6 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely right. The authors hypothesize that double descent is likely a consequence of poor estimators (OLS) in ill-posed regimes, not of the complexity measure. OLS can show double or multiple descent depending on the design, including in non-overparameterized regimes with peaks not at d/n=1. Tuned ridge keeps a U-shape and beats OLS. Switching to MDL-COMP does not remove double descent because MDL-COMP is monotone in d, though they still hold that parameter count is not a justified complexity measure.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear OLS and ridge regression sweeps and a discussion of MDL-COMP; it does not reproduce the original deep-network experiments or their training-time and data-size analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error behavior depends on estimator choice (OLS versus tuned ridge), covariate design (Gaussian versus cosine and other designs), and true model dimension relative to n. The authors report double or multiple descent for OLS depending on design and U-shaped curves for tuned ridge.
record.problems: The relevant empirical curves are for linear regression, not deep networks. Several Appendix D per-setting curves are available only as plots, without a textual assignment of the exact shape to each panel. The sample-size sweeps do not have a textual interpretation bearing on whether more data raises test error near interpolation. The discussion of MDL-COMP as an alternative axis is stated qualitatively rather than shown in a separate plot.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant outcomes were omitted. Cited double-descent findings from other studies and the paper's Prac-MDL-COMP-versus-CV/ARD/BIC model-selection comparisons were excluded because they do not report the claimed curve itself.

untested.parts: No deep networks; linear and kernel ridge only, and the NTK experiments report no capacity sweep.
Fig. B3 varies n with d fixed, but the text never states whether more data raises OLS test error near interpolation.
No test of a single complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.
Label noise is not varied (σ fixed). Truly optimal tuning is not tested, only CV- and Prac-MDL-COMP-tuned ridge.

missing.what: Bias-variance decomposition of OLS and tuned ridge test MSE. For OLS the variance term shows multiple design-dependent peaks that carry into test MSE; for ridge the variance rises then falls past d⋆.
Statement that OLS peaks can occur at d/n other than 1, and that double descent occurs in the non-overparameterized regime with ill-conditioned designs.
missing.locator: Appendix D intro; footnote 14 in Sec 6.1

record.verdict_notes: Removed the reader's V3 limits_scope label: rows r11-r13 cannot show the effect, so V3 is untested. Removed the V6 limits_scope label on r3-r6: its reasons (no label-noise test) describe untested parts, not limits. The OLS curves come from 50 noise redraws with no error bars. Original sources not involved.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments concern linear and kernel regression, not model-wise double descent in deep networks.
No test-error sweep over training epochs or training time is reported.

Appendix B3 varies sample size with fixed fitted-model dimension under three misspecifications, but the text does not state whether increasing sample size raises test error near the interpolation threshold. The plotted result is not sufficiently described to determine that direction.
Tests are limited to linear regression estimators and the reported settings; they do not establish a curve across all model classes.
The study does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and sample size.

The study compares OLS with tuned ridge and reports multiple descent under some designs, but does not isolate label noise as a cause, sweep noise levels to locate peaks, or test whether optimally tuned regularization eliminates every peak.

The authors discuss replacing parameter count with MDL-COMP and state that the qualitative conclusion is unchanged; they do not provide a separate plotted test-error curve with MDL-COMP on the horizontal axis.
